notes:
Renault Twingo III and the smart 453 (fortwo and forfour, the same platform, EQ electric variants included): 11-bit CAN at 500 kbit/s on the OBD-II socket, UDS, with the security gateway on a 29-bit identifier pair.

The units are every row of the CanZE 'Twingo_3_Ph2' ECU file, which lists petrol and electric units together (the engine and gearbox rows apply to combustion cars, the battery, charger and EVC rows to electric ones), each also present in the ddt4all address table. The file is for phase 2, so rows are unconfirmed for earlier Twingo III cars. No source read states that the smart 453 uses the same addresses: that rests on the shared platform and on ddt4all listing a Daimler smart project ('EDISON') whose address tables are identical to the Twingo's, so it is an inference and every smart row is unconfirmed. Treat every row as unconfirmed on a given car until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering.

The S-GW3 security gateway is listed on a 29-bit identifier pair (18DAF1D2 and 18DAD2F1, ISO 15765-4 29-bit normal fixed addressing) and nothing read states what it filters; units behind it may return no answer, which the tool reports as no response. The tool switches the adapter to the 29-bit protocol for that unit and back, at the same bit rate.

Session: the CanZE file gives 0x03 for every unit, which the guard permits, so the profile opens it; unconfirmed on a car.

Security gateway: a Renault security gateway is reported on recent cars, so a silent unit may be filtered rather than absent, and the tool reports a silent unit as no response, not as absent. A ddt4all issue (cedricp/ddt4all issue 404, Clio V, 2020) reports reads working through the OBD socket with writes blocked by a central gateway, and vendor pages (a Delphi article on a Renault Arkana, a Hella Gutmann page) say that fault codes and parameters can be read without unlocking it; none of them says which units a locked gateway hides from a read.
name: renault-twingo-smart-453
description: Renault Twingo III and smart 453 (fortwo and forfour), UDS over CAN, address plan from CanZE and ddt4all

vin.source: The WMIs are the makers' car and SUV identifiers in the world manufacturer identifier table of the Wikipedia article Vehicle identification number, which cites the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt manufacturer list SV 3.2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261102120229/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number). A WMI names the maker and plant, not the model, so a match only says the car is of a make this profile covers.
